items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Joe Dixon was in that band at the time.

ctx.x: And, so, we would go down and write together and talk and everything, and I would be doing my work, he would be doing his work. So, I took -- the first rehearsal we had in New York, I had my four arrangements and I took them down. So, Gus Arnheim says, "Just a minute, Budd, before you rehearse the band." Now, he said, "Gentlemen, I want you to know this now. Budd Johnson, as you know, is the musical director. He's the arranger for the band. And, if he tells me anybody can't play his music, then you better look…

He say, "So, I just want that understood, so you better pay close attention to him and see what he's got to tell you, you know." He gave me that respect. Well, of course, I mean, I never had no problem with the guys. You know what I mean. Because, I'm hanging out with them and having a ball. Joe Dixon was in that band at the time.
